# Rule catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs_counts.py. Edit the script, not this page. -->

ThreatCode ships 256 built-in rules in 58 rule files.
Severity is the base severity the rule assigns.
The engine can raise or lower it for a finding with a reason, as `effective_severity`, and the gate and the reports use that.
Confidence says how the rule knows: `definitive` when the configuration proves the condition, `heuristic` when it is inferred from names or partial data, and `absence` when it fires because something is missing.
ATT&CK tactics are derived from the techniques, so they are not listed per rule.

To write your own rules, see [Writing rules](writing-rules.md).

## Removed rules

These 29 rule ids existed in an earlier version and were removed, because the condition they tested did not describe an attacker's opportunity, tested an attribute that does not exist, or duplicated another rule.
Each is listed in the `deprecated_ids` of its rule file, so a `.threatcodeignore` line that still names one produces a warning instead of silently doing nothing.
